nonblocking_findings: F1 [Major] review-b: the folder refusal reads only the HTML and package hashes, so a re-render with the same sources replaces the approved PDF and contact sheet. Rationale: roundIdentity builds the identity from roundHtml and roundPackages only (make-proof-pdf.ts:46-51); the gate compares that identity and nothing else (make-proof-pdf.ts:85-92); the driver then writes the PDF into the same folder (make-proof-pdf.ts:107). The docstring claim 'an approved proof is never overwritten' (make-proof-pdf.ts:8-9) is therefore false for the PDF. Strategy step 4 requires 'refuse a hash mismatch', and that requirement is met in the letter. Fix: refuse when the target --out already exists, or add the PDF sha256 to the identity and use a new versioned folder for each round.

F2 [Nit] review-b: the driver blocks the unpkg.com CDN request by DNS mapping only, while the product print scripts remove the script tag. Rationale: make-proof-pdf.ts:104 maps unpkg.com to ~NOTFOUND; the proof HTML keeps the tag with no integrity attribute (1 script element, 0 integrity= matches, 0 iframe elements); make-book-pdf.ts:60 and make-lesson-pdfs.ts:79 strip the tag before render. If a Chrome channel change or a proxy ignores the mapping, third-party JavaScript runs on the proof page. Fix: strip the tag in the driver as the product scripts do, in addition to the mapping.

F3 [Nit] review-b: P9 matches one exact file name, so a Quest 5 printer file under any other name passes the gate. Rationale: check_p9 walks ~/Desktop/print-ready for the exact name only (checks.py:247-252). I found 0 files with 'quest-5', 'quest5', or 'quest_5' outside the proof folder, and 52 PDFX files that belong to other books, so the current gate result stands. Fix: match the prefix 'Primary-Advantage-Quest-5'.

F4 [Nit] review-b: the two Thai proof HTML files sit inside the public repository working tree and no .gitignore rule covers them. Rationale: quest5-l01.html holds 1,035,899 bytes and 1167 Thai characters, and adventure92-l09.html holds 1,040,560 bytes and 2001 Thai characters; git ls-files returns 0 and git status shows both as untracked; checks.py:195-198 catches a staged file through the index; .gitignore holds no rule for proof HTML, so a later 'git add -A' in another session commits them. The Thai text is already public in content/primary/quest-5/l01.json (1147 characters, tracked) and content/primary/adventure-9.2/l09.json (2029 characters, tracked), so the residual risk is repository noise and local path exposure, not a new content leak. Fix: add the two file names to .gitignore.
